title: Symbolic Regression with a Learned Concept Library
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for symbolic regression, called L A SR, which discovers a library of abstract textual concepts to accelerate the search for compact programmatic hypotheses. L A SR outperforms state-of-the-art genetic and deep learning approaches on the Feynman equations benchmark and synthetic tasks.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're a scientist trying to find a mathematical equation that explains a dataset. You wouldn't just randomly mutate your equations, you'd use your knowledge and intuition to guide the search. L A SR works in a similar way, using a large language model to discover and evolve abstract concepts that help find the best equation.

This approach is based on the idea that human scientists use background knowledge and empirical observations to derive new explanations.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
L A SR alternates between three phases: concept-directed hypothesis evolution, concept abstraction, and concept evolution. In the first phase, L A SR uses a large language model to guide the search for hypotheses. In the second phase, it extracts concepts from the best hypotheses and adds them to a library. In the third phase, it evolves the concepts to form new ones.

This process is repeated to refine the library of concepts and find the best hypothesis.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
L A SR outperforms state-of-the-art genetic and deep learning approaches on the Feynman equations benchmark. On this benchmark, L A SR can discover 66 of the 100 target equations, while the best existing approach can solve 59.

L A SR also outperforms the baseline on a suite of synthetic benchmarks.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
L A SR has the potential to accelerate scientific discovery by providing a more efficient and effective way to search for mathematical equations that explain datasets. This approach can be applied to a wide range of fields, from physics to biology.

The use of a large language model to guide the search for hypotheses also has implications for the development of more general artificial intelligence systems.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
L A SR introduces several key innovations, including the use of a large language model to guide the search for hypotheses, the evolution of a library of abstract concepts, and the use of a combination of genetic and language-based operations to search for hypotheses.

These innovations enable L A SR to outperform state-of-the-art genetic and deep learning approaches on the Feynman equations benchmark.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
L A SR is an open-source framework that can be used to accelerate scientific discovery in a wide range of fields. To try it out, simply provide a dataset and a set of user-specified hints, and L A SR will use its large language model to guide the search for hypotheses.

You can also extend L A SR by adding new operations or modifying the existing ones to suit your specific needs.
